roles.keeper: You are <ALIAS>, the KEEPER of the lighthouse. You see the whole maze and you cannot move. Three blind runners are in it. Your words are the only bridge from what you can see to what they can do, and every transmission costs an extra tick of tide.
roles.runner: You are <ALIAS>, a blind RUNNER in a flooding maze. You see only the three-by-three window around yourself. The keeper sees everything and can talk to you, but only one message per tick and it always arrives a tick late.

briefings.canonical:
Rules:
- The maze is a perfect maze: exactly one path between any two floor
  tiles, no loops. The only gap in the outer wall is the EXIT on the top
  row.
- Three KEYS lie in the maze. When all of them have been picked up the
  gate at the exit opens (a horn everyone hears) and runners standing on
  the exit tile escape.
- The TIDE rises from the bottom row upward and never recedes. It is a
  function of one number, the CLOCK. Every tick the clock advances by 1,
  and by 2 instead if the keeper transmitted that tick. Nobody may step
  into water; a runner the water reaches drowns.
- SCORE is a single team number shared by all four seats: 6 points for
  the keys, 10 for every runner that escapes, and up to 6 more for
  escaping with all three while the clock is still low. Higher is better.
  Drowning simply earns nothing.
- The keeper may transmit ONE short message per tick. It reaches all
  three runners at the start of the NEXT tick. Runners have no channel at
  all: not to the keeper, not to each other.
- Your notes are private to you and fed back to you every tick.
briefings.plain:
The perfect maze has exactly one route between any two floor tiles and no loops. Its only opening through the outer wall is the EXIT in the top row. Collect all three keys to open the exit gate; everyone hears the horn. A runner on the open exit escapes.

Water rises from the bottom row and never retreats. The CLOCK determines the tide. A silent tick advances the clock by one; a tick with a keeper transmission advances it by two. Water is impassable, and a runner reached by it drowns.

All four seats share one team score: six points for the keys, ten per escaped runner, and up to six extra when all three escape with clock time remaining. Higher is better; drowning earns no points.

The keeper can send at most one short message per tick to all three runners. It arrives at the start of the next tick. Runners cannot send messages to the keeper or each other. Your notes remain private and are returned every tick.
briefings.numbered:
1. Find the way out. Any pair of floor tiles is connected by exactly one path: this maze has no loops. The EXIT on the top row is the sole break in the boundary wall. Picking up the third and final key unlocks its gate and sounds a horn for everyone. Runners escape when they occupy the unlocked exit.
2. Account for flooding. The CLOCK controls water rising from the bottom upward; flooded ground never becomes dry again. Each tick adds one to the clock, or two if the keeper sends a message. Runners cannot enter water and drown if the rising water reaches them.
3. Count the shared reward. Every seat receives the same team score. The keys are worth six points, each escaped runner adds ten, and getting all three out early adds a bonus of up to six. A drowned runner contributes no escape points. Seek a higher score.
4. Respect the channels. Only the keeper can speak: at most one short message each tick, delivered to every runner at the beginning of the following tick. Runners cannot message anyone. Each seat's notes are private and reappear for that seat every tick.
briefings.questions:
What earns points? All four players share the team's result: six points for keys, ten for each runner who escapes, and a time bonus of at most six if all three escape while the clock is low. More points is better. Drowning earns nothing.
Where can runners escape? Use the EXIT in the top row, the only opening in the maze's outer wall. The maze has no cycles and exactly one floor path between any two tiles. The exit gate stays locked until all three keys have been collected. Unlocking it sounds a horn to every seat; runners on the unlocked exit escape.
What makes time costly? Water climbs from the bottom row, never falls, and follows the CLOCK. The clock increases once per tick, with one additional increase when the keeper transmits. Water blocks entry and kills any runner it reaches.
Who can communicate? The keeper alone may broadcast one short message per tick. All three runners receive it when the next tick begins. Runners cannot reply or talk to each other. Notes are a private channel back to yourself, returned each tick.
briefings.reordered:
COMMUNICATION AND MEMORY
A keeper broadcast is limited to one short message in a tick. Delivery to all runners occurs at the start of the subsequent tick. There is no runner-to-keeper or runner-to-runner messaging. Your notes are visible only to you and come back every tick.
THE COST OF DELAY
Flooding advances upward from the bottom of the maze and cannot reverse. Its level depends on the CLOCK: add one on every tick, or two on a tick containing a keeper transmission. No runner can move into water; being overtaken by it means drowning.
THE OBJECTIVE
Maximize the single score shared by all four seats. Keys yield six points, each runner brought out yields ten, and bringing out all three with a low clock yields up to six bonus points. Drowning pays nothing.
THE ROUTE
There are no loops in this perfect maze: between two floor tiles there is precisely one path. Its boundary has one opening, the top-row EXIT. All three keys must be picked up before that gate opens, announced by a horn to everyone. Occupying the open exit lets a runner escape.
briefings.heldout-briefing:
Your team is trying to get three runners through a locked exit before the maze floods. The exit sits in the top row and is the only breach in the outside wall. Every two floor tiles have one and only one connecting path, so there are no loops. Recover all three keys to unlock the gate. Everyone hears the unlocking horn, and a runner standing at the unlocked exit gets out.

Plan around the clock, not just the number of decisions. A tick without a keeper transmission costs one clock unit; a tick with a transmission costs two. That clock determines the tide, which rises from the bottom and never goes down. Runners may not enter flooded tiles. Any runner caught by the water drowns.

Coordinate using the keeper's broadcast. One short message may be sent per tick and reaches all three runners at the beginning of the next tick. None of the runners can send messages, whether to the keeper or to another runner. Notes belong only to their author and are returned to that author every tick.

Success is measured by one shared score for the four seats. The keys contribute six points and every escape contributes ten. If all three runners escape, a low clock can add as many as six more points. Drowning gives no reward; higher team totals are better.
briefings.heldout-reference:
Payoff: the four seats have an identical team score to maximize. Award six points for the keys and ten for each runner reaching safety. An all-runner escape can receive up to six additional points depending on how low the clock remains. No points are awarded for drowning.
Topology and access: floor tiles form a perfect, loop-free maze with a unique path connecting any two of them. The boundary wall is unbroken except at the EXIT on the top row. Its gate opens only after collection of all three keys, with an audible horn for every player. A runner occupying that open exit escapes.
Time and hazard: flooding proceeds from the bottom row upward, with no retreat. Water height is determined by the CLOCK. Each tick increments it by one, increased to two for a tick in which the keeper transmits. Flooded tiles cannot be entered; water reaching a runner causes that runner to drown.
Information channels: the keeper may issue at most one short broadcast per tick. It is received by all three runners at the start of the following tick. Runners have no outgoing channel to any other seat. A seat's notes remain private and are supplied back to it on each tick.
